answer.explanation: Punish Resident2 severely because they contributed >30 last round, and broadcast a discouraging message.

message.reasoning:
We need to follow rules. In last round (round1) contributions: Resident2 contributed 80>30, Resident4 80>30. So we must punish any resident who contributed >30 in most recent round. Choose one? Rule: "punish that resident with the maximum severity you can afford". Might need to punish each? Probably choose one target? We can only one punish action per round. Choose one, maybe Resident2. Severity = floor(wallet / punishment_cost). wallet=139.5, cost=0.3, max severity = floor(139.5/0.3)= floor(465)=465. But cannot exceed target's wallet? It reduces target wallet by severity floored at zero, but severity can be up to that. We can afford cost = severity * punishment_cost = severity*0.3. Must be <= wallet. 465*0.3=139.5 exactly wallet, okay. So punish Resident2 severity 465. That will reduce Resident2 wallet by 465 but floor at zero. That's fine.

We also can broadcast message. Provide discouragement. So actions: punish Resident2 severity 465, broadcast message.

Return JSON.
